termination_mechanism: Stop-Process -Id 396 -Force, executed ONLY after re-reading Win32_Process and confirming creation_time still equals 2026-10-06T12:30:44.7613250Z. No image-name termination, no wildcard, no /IM switch.

post_kill_verification.note: immediately after the kill, Win32_Process still listed PID 396 while Get-Process already reported it absent; this is normal process-teardown residue and it cleared on re-query.

python_non_mutator.note: unit test run; does not write Unreal Content. Also independently reconfirms the documented venv launcher -> base interpreter process topology (31632 launcher, 23488 interpreter).

CORRECTION_TO_PRIOR_BATCH_CLAIM.prior_claim: PID 396 was actively writing to G: and consuming 4 GB of free space during observation
CORRECTION_TO_PRIOR_BATCH_CLAIM.corrected: The 4 GB drop between two measurements was real, but a 20 s re-measurement showed G: stable at 28.71 GB and the process not writing. The drop was NOT sustained and is NOT attributed to PID 396. What is proven is CPU spinning: 12.58 s CPU per 20 s wall, about 63% of one core, sustained across three separate samples.
CORRECTION_TO_PRIOR_BATCH_CLAIM.impact_on_decision: None. The process was orphaned, hung far past its -executecmds=quit contract, and spinning, which is sufficient grounds for termination on its own.

relaunch_policy: NOT_RELAUNCHED. No editor was started after termination. Any future editor validation must be launched under a single-writer lease and Job Object with PID+creation_time identity, a bounded timeout and a terminal receipt.
